newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - British business press - Oct 14.

text.p: Prepared by The Broadcast Monitoring Company for Reuters
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- WARBURG TOP STAFF WIN LOYALTY PAY

SBC Warburg, the investment bank, has paid 'lock-in' bonuses to some of its senior executives which amounts to more than 100 per cent of basic salary in some cases. The bonus scheme has been set up as a way of preventing its key staff defecting to rival organisations. Insiders believe that the average payment will represent around 50 per cent of salary.
-- SIGNET IN TALKS WITH REBELS ON CAPITAL RESTRUCTURING

Signet, the jewellery chain, is in talks with its rebel shareholders in an attempt to reorganise its highly complex capital structure. The group is also under pressure as its banking facilities of 320 million stg expire next June.
-- PRISM SEEKS 13 MILLION POUNDS FROM RIGHTS ISSUE

Prism, the train operator, is hoping to raise around 13 million stg in a rights issue today as it takes over the running of South Wales and West and Cardiff railways. The issue will be at 240p and is expected to be a 5-for-13 rights offer of about 5.5 million new shares.
THE TIMES
-- FUND MANAGERS FORECAST RISE IN INFLATION AND INTEREST RATES

The latest Merrill Lynch Gallup survey shows that 99 per cent of the fund managers surveyed are expecting higher inflation in a year's time, due to strengthening economic growth. Over the same period, 89 per cent of those questioned believe base rates will also rise. Most fund managers are thought to be working on the assumption that Kenneth Clarke will not raise base rates before a spring election for political reasons.
-- OFFICIALS PAID BRIBES ESCAPE PROSECUTION

The head of the Audit Commission states that attempts by government officials to pressurise people into paying them bribes should be treated as "maladministration" rather than "corruption", which means that evidence from the government officials should be sent to the Government Ombudsman whose powers are only to award compensation, and not the Crown Prosecution Service, which could start criminal proceedings. -- SEVEN TO GO AS INSIDER TAKES REINS AT MGAM

Keith Percy the chief executive of Morgan Grenfell Asset Management is to be replaced later this week by Robert Smith who currently heads the development capital division of Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. The total number of resignations this week is expected to be seven. The departures follow the completion of a preliminary report into the Morgan Grenfell affair by Ernst & Young.
THE GUARDIAN
-- SOLICITORS' REPORT ON WICKES 'WILL GO TO SFO'

A report out this week into how Wickes, the DIY chain, overstated profits by 50 million stg, is expected to be studied by the Serious Fraud Office. The report by City solicitors Linklaters & Paine, is thought to list a series of irregular accounting practices. Wickes is prepared to hand over a copy of the report if a request is made by the SFO.
-- JUDGE BLOCKS FOX NEWS FROM NYC CABLE

Rupert Murdoch yesterday lost a legal battle that will keep his Fox News channel off Time Warner's cable system in New York City. A federal judge blocked Mayor Rudolf Giuliani's attempt to get Fox News on one of the City's public access channels. The judge granted Time Warner's request for a temporary restraining order, after finding that the city had violated federal law in trying to control what goes on air.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- CRACKDOWN ON SCHEMES TO AVOID BONUS TAX

The authorities are to crack down on schemes designed to reduce the tax paid on bonuses to bankers and other professionals and have already challenged one technique used by investment banks to avoid National Insurance contributions by paying bonuses in the form of life policies that are subsequently cashed in. The Department of Social Security, which is responsible for National Insurance contributions, is thought to be collecting material to begin a court action against other tax reduction plans.
-- UTILITY JOB CUTS 'COST TAXPAYER 805 MILLION POUNDS'

A study produced by the Labour Party to justify its proposed windfall profits tax suggests that privatised utilities had cut 89,473 jobs since the last election at a cost of 805 million stg to the taxpayer. The study reveals that there has been a substantial payback to shareholders and a growing payout by taxpayers who pick up the cost of unemployment benefits and lost revenue.
-- VNU FORCES HOLLICK TO MAKE DECISION ON BLENHEIM

Chief executive of United News and Media, Lord Hollick, is expected to make a decision this morning on whether to intervene in the struggle for Blenheim Exhibitions. Dutch publishing group VNU is thought to be looking to lift its stake in Blenheim from the 14.9 per cent it acquired last week to a possible 29.9 per cent. It is this that has forced Lord Hollick's hand. A bid would cost United at least 480 million, but it is likely to proceed with caution as a bid war could prove expensive.
